Best crypto inheritance tools (2026)

By the Afterkeep research team · Reviewed on 15 Oct 2026 · Independent: sponsors can't buy a verdict · How we rate

Casa and Unchained are the strongest choices for Bitcoin inheritance using multisig. Vault12 Guard suits people with many wallets who want social-recovery seed backup. Ledger Recover is a recovery service first and an inheritance tool second.

Key facts

  • #1 Casa: Bitcoin holders who want self-custody plus a guided inheritance plan.
  • #2 Unchained: Larger Bitcoin holdings, especially in the US, where a formal inheritance process is worth paying for.
  • #3 Vault12 Guard: Self-custody users with many wallets who don't want a seed phrase stored in one place.
  • #4 Ledger Recover: Ledger owners worried about losing their seed phrase who accept ID verification.
  • #5 Bitkey: Bitcoin holders who want simple self-custody with inheritance built in.
  • #6 Nunchuk: Bitcoin holders who want timelock-based inheritance without KYC.
  • #7 Liana: Technical bitcoin holders who want DIY inheritance with no company holding keys.
  • #8 AnchorWatch: Larger bitcoin holders who want insured, documented inheritance.

Quick picks

  • Best overall: Casa (Top pick) · Paid
  • Runner-up: Unchained (Good) · Paid
  • Also good: Vault12 Guard (Good) · Paid

Which should you choose?

1. Casa Official site ↗

Best for: Bitcoin holders who want self-custody plus a guided inheritance plan.

A leading multisig self-custody service with inheritance included in every plan, covering bitcoin, ETH and stablecoins.

Pricing: From $250/yr (Standard); Premium $2,100/yr; Private Client $7,500/yr (USD). Check current pricing.

2. Unchained Official site ↗

Best for: Larger Bitcoin holdings, especially in the US, where a formal inheritance process is worth paying for.

Collaborative-custody Bitcoin vaults (2-of-3 multisig) with inheritance planning. Strong for larger holdings.

Pricing: Check current pricing.

3. Vault12 Guard Official site ↗

Best for: Self-custody users with many wallets who don't want a seed phrase stored in one place.

Backs up seed phrases using trusted 'Guardians' and lets you name a beneficiary who can inherit after a 48-hour owner veto window and Guardian approvals.

Pricing: Check current pricing.

4. Ledger Recover Official site ↗

Best for: Ledger owners worried about losing their seed phrase who accept ID verification.

An optional, ID-based seed backup for Ledger hardware wallets. Handy for recovery, but it's a trust trade-off and isn't primarily an inheritance tool.

Pricing: Paid subscription (Ledger has advertised $9.99/month). Check current pricing.

5. Bitkey Official site ↗

Best for: Bitcoin holders who want simple self-custody with inheritance built in.

A bitcoin-only 2-of-3 multisig wallet with built-in inheritance: your beneficiary starts a claim, and funds unlock only after a 6-month delay you can cancel.

Pricing: Hardware listed at $250 on bitkey.world. Check current pricing.

6. Nunchuk Official site ↗

Best for: Bitcoin holders who want timelock-based inheritance without KYC.

A non-custodial bitcoin inheritance platform: Nunchuk holds one key it can't use alone, and a timelock unlocks funds for your beneficiary on the date you set.

Pricing: Free DIY wallets; the inheritance plan (Honey Badger) is listed at 480/year. Check current pricing and currency.

7. Liana Official site ↗

Best for: Technical bitcoin holders who want DIY inheritance with no company holding keys.

A free, open-source bitcoin wallet from Wizardsardine with time-based recovery paths, so a family member or trusted contact can access funds if something happens to you.

Pricing: Liana Wallet is free and open source; Liana Business is a paid service.

8. AnchorWatch Official site ↗

Best for: Larger bitcoin holders who want insured, documented inheritance.

Bitcoin custody with an Inheritance Protocol and estate documentation for your attorney, plus optional Lloyd's of London insurance for US customers.

Pricing: Check official pricing.
